title: Kyverno 1.10 (Helm chart v3) cannot be upgraded in place from chart v2 — the controllers were split and renamed

detection.reason: the chart v2 admission controller Deployment is named after the release (`kyverno`, `<release>-kyverno`); chart v3 names every controller `*-admission-controller` / `*-background-controller` / …, so a Deployment ending in `kyverno` running the Kyverno image is a v2-era install (a v2 release named e.g. `kyverno-prod` is not matched — the verify command lists every Kyverno Deployment)

quote: Direct upgrades from v2 of the Helm chart to v3 are not supported due to the number of breaking changes and manual intervention is required.
remediation: Plan a maintenance window: either back up every Kyverno policy (`kubectl get pol,cpol,cleanpol,ccleanpol,polex -A -o yaml`), uninstall, install chart v3 and restore, or scale `kyverno` to zero and upgrade with `--set upgrade.fromV2=true`. Before uninstalling, set `generate.synchronize: false` on data-type generate rules or the uninstall deletes their generated resources; after restoring, add `spec.generateExisting: true` to refresh them. Translate your values to the v3 names first (see the chart-values card). Raw YAML installs have no upgrade path: uninstall with the old manifest, install the new one.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)kyverno/(kyverno|background-controller|cleanup-controller|reports-controller)([:@]|$)"))) | select(.metadata.name | test("-controller$") | not) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a Kyverno Deployment not named *-controller: a chart v2 install

title: Chart v3 renamed or moved most values — a v2 values file is silently ignored where a key moved
quote: In `v3` chart values changed significantly, please read the instructions below to migrate your values:
remediation: Translate every value you set to its v3 name before upgrading: `replicaCount` → `admissionController.replicas`, `installCRDs` → `crds.install`, `namespace` → `namespaceOverride`, `image`/`resources`/`extraArgs`/`envVars` → `admissionController.container.*` (extraArgs become an object, not an array), `config.excludeUsername` → `config.excludeUsernames`, `config.excludeGroupRole` → `config.excludeGroups`, `generatecontrollerExtraResources` → `admissionController.rbac.clusterRole.extraResources`, and the rest of the list in the chart README. Image tags must be quoted strings, and an overridden registry goes in `image.registry`.
verifyCommand: helm list -A -o json | jq -r '.[] | select(.chart | test("^kyverno-[0-9]")) | "\(.namespace)/\(.name) \(.chart) app \(.app_version)"'  # each row is a Kyverno Helm release; read its values with: helm get values NAME -n NAMESPACE
coversNotes: v1.10.0 Helm: The namespace field is renamed to namespaceOverride (#6065)
v1.10.0 Helm: #6586 fix: remove obsolete generatecontrollerExtraResources from helm chart

title: Aggregated ClusterRoles must carry the new per-controller aggregation labels
quote: As a result of this decomposition, aggregated ClusterRoles may need to be updated to use the new label values depending on the controller which requires those permissions.
remediation: Find every ClusterRole you wrote to extend Kyverno's permissions (for generate or mutate-existing rules on extra resources) and relabel it for the controller that now needs it — the background controller for generate and mutate-existing, the admission controller for admission-time lookups, the reports controller for background scans. Without the new label the permission is not aggregated and those policies are refused or fail.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.metadata.labels // {}) | to_entries | any(.key | test("kyverno"))) | "\(.metadata.name) \((.metadata.labels // {}) | to_entries | map(select(.key | test("kyverno")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(","))"'  # each row is a ClusterRole carrying a Kyverno label; check the aggregation label names its controller

title: Policies matching subresource kinds such as PodExecOptions must use the `Pod/exec` form

detection.reason: read from the kinds named in each policy's match/exclude blocks (case-sensitive: the new parent form `Deployment/scale` names the subresource in lower case)

quote: Policies which matched on some types of subresources (such as `PodExecOptions`) will need to be updated to use the standardized form of `<parent>/<subresource>` (`Pod/exec`).
remediation: Rewrite each match on a subresource's own kind to its parent form — `PodExecOptions` → `Pod/exec`, `PodAttachOptions` → `Pod/attach`, `Eviction` → `Pod/eviction`, `Scale` → `Deployment/scale` (or the parent you meant). 1.10 refuses the old form when the policy is created or updated, and a policy matching a subresource must set `background: false`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.rules[]? | (.match, .exclude) | .. | .kinds? // empty | .[]] | any(test("^([^ ]+/)?(PodExecOptions|PodAttachOptions|PodPortForwardOptions|PodProxyOptions|NodeProxyOptions|ServiceProxyOptions|Eviction|Binding|Scale|TokenRequest)$"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row matches a subresource kind by its own name
coversNotes: v1.10.0 Changed: Changed matching syntax when it comes to subresources
v1.10.0 Changed: Policies matching on subresources are now properly rejected

title: Generate rules: several fields are immutable, variables are refused in clone/kind/apiVersion, and `generate.apiVersion` is required

detection.reason: which generate fields carry variables or a missing apiVersion is not collected

quote: The following fields in a generate rule are now immutable once created:
remediation: For each policy with a generate rule: set `generate.apiVersion` if it is missing, remove variables from `clone`, `cloneList`, `generate.kind` and `generate.apiVersion`, and expect edits to `rules.name`, `match`, `exclude`, `preconditions` and the generate target (apiVersion, kind, namespace, name, clone) to be refused — delete and recreate the policy to change them. From 1.10.2 the target's scope is checked too: `generate.namespace` set on a cluster-scoped kind ("target namespace must not be set for a cluster-wide resource") or missing on a namespaced kind ("target namespace must be set for a namespaced resource") is refused. Policies breaking any of these are rejected on create/update, so re-applying an unchanged manifest from Git starts failing.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.rules[]?; has("generate"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row has a generate rule; check apiVersion is set, clone/kind/apiVersion carry no {{ }}, and namespace is set exactly when the kind is namespaced
coversNotes: v1.10.0: Variables in these portions of a generate rule

title: Generate and mutate-existing policies are refused when Kyverno lacks the permissions to act on their targets

detection.reason: Kyverno's effective RBAC is not collected

quote: Generate and "mutate existing" policies, once installed, will check to see if Kyverno has the necessary permissions to successfully execute them.
remediation: Before upgrading, grant the background controller the verbs on every resource your generate and mutate-existing rules write (an aggregated ClusterRole labelled for the background controller). 1.10 also narrows the chart's default permissions, so a policy that worked through a broad default role is now refused at creation.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.rules[]?; has("generate") or (.mutate.targets? != null))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row needs background-controller permissions on its targets

title: `mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true` now requires `mutate.targets[]` or the policy is refused

detection.reason: whether each mutate rule defines targets is not collected

quote: also has `mutate.targets[]` defined or else the policy creation will be blocked
remediation: Add `mutate.targets[]` to every mutate rule of a policy that sets `mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true`, or drop the flag.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate == true) | select(any(.spec.rules[]?; has("mutate") and (.mutate.targets == null))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row sets mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate with a mutate rule that has no targets

title: A verifyImages policy in Audit mode is refused unless `mutateDigest: false`

detection.reason: verifyImages rule fields are not collected

quote: When a verifyImages policy is created in `Audit` mode, its creation will be rejected unless `mutateDigest` is set to `false` (#6757)
remediation: Set `mutateDigest: false` on every verifyImages rule of a policy whose failure action is Audit.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.validationFailureAction // "" | test("(?i)audit")) and any(.spec.rules[]?.verifyImages[]?; .mutateDigest != false)) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is an Audit policy whose verifyImages rule does not set mutateDigest: false

title: The ConfigMap keys `excludeGroupRole` / `excludeUsername` are renamed `excludeGroups` / `excludeUsernames` — the old ones are ignored

detection.reason: reads the key names of the kyverno ConfigMap

remediation: Rename the keys in the `kyverno` ConfigMap (1.9 read excludeGroupRole / excludeUsername, pkg/config/config.go@v1.9.5; 1.10 reads only excludeGroups / excludeUsernames). With the old keys every exclusion silently disappears — requests from system:nodes and the identities you exempted are evaluated by policies.
verifyCommand: kubectl get cm -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "kyverno") | select(.data | has("excludeGroupRole") or has("excludeUsername")) | .metadata.namespace'  # each row is a Kyverno ConfigMap still using the old key names

title: `--genWorkers` and the background-scan flags are no longer flags of the admission controller

detection.reason: checked in the container args of the Kyverno Deployments (admission controller) — a flag passed any other way is not scanned

quote: Removed the `--genWorker` flag from the admission controller as this is only applicable to the background controller. (#7132)
remediation: 1.10 splits Kyverno into four controllers and the admission controller stops accepting the flags that moved with them: `--genWorkers` (now the background controller's) and `--backgroundScan`, `--backgroundScanWorkers`, `--backgroundScanInterval`, `--reportsChunkSize` (now the reports controller's; cmd/kyverno/main.go@v1.9.5 vs cmd/{background,reports}-controller/main.go@v1.10.0). Remove them from the admission controller's extra args and set them on the controller that owns them; an unknown flag stops the container at start.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)kyverno/(kyverno|background-controller|cleanup-controller|reports-controller)([:@]|$)"))) | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]?; test("^--?(genWorkers?|backgroundScan(Workers|Interval)?|reportsChunkSize)(=|$)"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row passes a flag that moved to another controller in 1.10 (meaningful on a 1.9 install, where one Deployment runs everything)

title: foreach mutations: patches are combined at the end, loops run top-down, and autogen is off for JSON-patch foreach rules

detection.reason: foreach mutate rule contents are not collected

quote: When using multiple `foreach` loops, they will be evaluated from top down so the result of one loop will only be available to the next after the first loop completes.
remediation: Re-test mutate rules with several `foreach` loops (one loop no longer sees another's patches until it finishes) and set `foreach.order` where the order matters. A foreach mutation using JSON patches no longer gets an autogen copy for Pod controllers — add explicit Deployment/StatefulSet rules if you relied on it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.rules[]?.mutate?; .foreach != null)) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row has a foreach mutation

title: Background scans now skip resources excluded by resourceFilters (new default)

detection.reason: the reports controller's effective flags are not decisive on their own

quote: Added new flag `skipResourceFilters` to reports controller to enable/disable considering resource filters in the background (default value is `true`)
remediation: Expect MORE background PolicyReport results: with the new default `true` the reports controller ignores the ConfigMap's resourceFilters (pkg/config/config.go@v1.10.0: filters apply only when skipResourceFilters is false), so filtered resources are reported.
